newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil plans ethylene plant at Kaarstoe.
newsitem.headline: Statoil plans ethylene plant at Kaarstoe.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it planned to build a production plant, storage tank and export facility for ethylene at the Kaarstoe gas treatment complex north of Stavanger.

Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said the expansion follows a contract between the licensees of the North Sea Troll development and a buyer group covering annual deliveries of roughly 600,000 tonnes of ethylene from 2000.
Ethylene is one of the building-block feedstocks for the petrochemical industry.
The Troll licence group, comprising Statoil, Shell, Norsk Hydro, Saga Petroleum, Elf, Conoco and Total, also has signed several deals with other fields supplying gas to Kaarstoe.
Statoil said the buyer group was made up of the joint-venture Borealis petrochemical group, which is 50/50 pct owned by Statoil and Finland's Neste Oy, Noretyl and Norsk Hydro.
The contract is conditional upon approval by the boards of each company and the necessary official permits.
